title: Trinity: A General Purpose FHE Accelerator
problem: No single FHE accelerator efficiently supports both arithmetic FHE (CKKS) and logic FHE (TFHE) schemes simultaneously, and prior ASIC-based accelerators support only one scheme with none supporting FHE scheme conversion, requiring multiple separate accelerators that increase system complexity.
motivation: Fully Homomorphic Encryption enables privacy-preserving computation directly on encrypted data without decryption, which is critical for privacy-sensitive applications.
method: Trinity decomposes CKKS, TFHE, and their conversion schemes into finite arithmetic kernels (NTT, FFT, MAC) and implements a unified ASIC architecture supporting them concurrently. It employs dynamic workload scheduling, adaptive NTT/MAC component allocation, and hardware component reuse to maintain high utilization across variable polynomial lengths and diverse arithmetic workloads.
key_novelty: First unified multi-modal FHE accelerator supporting CKKS, TFHE, and conversion schemes within a single architecture instead of requiring multiple separate accelerators.
contributions: First multi-modal FHE accelerator with unified architecture supporting CKKS, TFHE, and FHE-conversion schemes simultaneously
Novel algorithmic and architectural solutions enabling concurrent NTT/FFT, maintaining utilization across polynomial lengths, and supporting diverse arithmetic kernels
Dynamic workload scheduling and adaptive component allocation achieving 1.49x speedup over SHARP (CKKS) and 4.23x over Morphling (TFHE)
919.3x performance improvement for FHE-conversion over CPU while using only 85% of the combined hardware area of SHARP and Morphling

metrics.speedup: 1.49x vs SHARP (CKKS), 4.23x vs Morphling (TFHE), 919.3x vs CPU (conversion)
metrics.area: 85% of summed circuit areas of SHARP and Morphling
